column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) said: “Allah the Exalted is pure (ṭayyib) and accepts only what is pure. Allah has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, for He said:

‘O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds’ [al-Muʾminūn 23:51], and the Exalted said: ‘O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided you’ [al-Baqarah 2:172].” Then he mentioned a man who travels far, dishevelled and covered in dust, stretching his hands towards the sky: “O Lord! O Lord!”
—“while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful and he has been nourished with the unlawful; so how can he be answered?” Reported by Muslim.
His words, “Allah the Exalted is pure and accepts only what is pure”, show that al-Ṭayyib (the Pure) is one of the names of Allah, and that He accepts deeds that are characterised by purity.
This is general for all deeds, including earning: a person should do only what is righteous, earn only what is pure and spend only from what is pure.
His words, “Allah has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, for He said: ‘O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds’, and the Exalted said:

‘O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided you’”: in these two verses the messengers and those to whom they were sent are commanded to eat of the good things. Just as the messengers eat only what is pure, their followers must eat only what is pure.
His words, “Then he mentioned a man who travels far, dishevelled and covered in dust, stretching his hands towards the sky: O Lord! O Lord!

—while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful and he has been nourished with the unlawful; so how can he be answered?”: having made clear that Allah accepts only what is pure, and that the messengers and the believers have been commanded to eat of the good things,
the Prophet ﷺ made clear that some people go against this way: their food is not pure; rather, they deliberately earn the unlawful and use it in all their affairs, in food, clothing and nourishment,

and that this is among the causes of his supplication not being accepted, even though he has brought about the causes for a supplication to be accepted. In this hadith these are four: travelling, and travelling far; being dishevelled and dusty;

stretching out his hands in supplication; and calling on Allah by His lordship, persisting with his Lord by repeating it. The meaning of his words, “so how can he be answered?”, is that an answer is unlikely, because of the presence of causes that prevent the supplication from being accepted.
Al-Ṭayyib (the Pure) is one of the names of Allah, meaning the One free of deficiencies, and purity (ṭīb) is one of His attributes,
since all the names of Allah are derived and indicate attributes derived from them.
A Muslim should bring what is pure in his deeds and his earnings.

Charity is accepted only from lawful wealth. It is established that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah does not accept a prayer without purification, nor charity from stolen spoils.” Reported by Muslim (224).
Allah's favour to His servants with blessings, and His commanding them to eat of the good things.
Eating what is unlawful is among the causes of supplication not being accepted.
Among the causes of supplication being accepted are travel and the supplicant's being dishevelled and dusty.
Also among the causes of its acceptance is raising the hands in supplication.
Also among its causes is seeking nearness [to Allah] through His names.
Among its causes is persisting with Allah in it.
